design: Designed for the open pack, from history and sailing physics; nothing from the original game.  Speeds: a square-rig polar (best on the quarter, lying six points off the wind, taken aback head to wind) and a fore-and-aft one (best from the beam to a close reach, making some way into the wind by short tacks) blended per class by its rig and scaled by its best speed, from 7 for the sloops and pinnaces (8 for the Jamaica sloops from 1640) to 5 for the galleons, so the fastest class outsails the slowest by about half again off the wind and two to four times close-hauled; square rigs gain weatherliness by era (0.4 here).  Ships met: per region five archetypes from the least to the most dangerous, chosen for the era's history (the Anglo-Dutch and Franco-Dutch wars: the stormiest politics, buccaneers at their boldest); since most sails are met far from a town, where all twenty records are equally likely, the era's sea traffic is their census by flag (Spain, England, France, Holland, pirates: 5, 4, 4, 3, 4), one pirate per region; navies scaled x1.10, raiders' role +2, Spanish gold x0.80, goods x1.20; the treasure galleon's gold factor 50.  Enemy captain: strength = 2 x hull + guns + crew comparison + nerve 1; he boards when ahead with the stronger crew, lies broadside when ahead, runs when behind or holed.  Diplomacy range 60, Spanish shipwrights' tolerance 95 (loosening as Spain's monopoly weakens).
